title: Carwyn's Big, Busy Bell
markdown:
The sun burst through Bramble the badger’s window, quick bright gold, colours dancing in the burrow. He stretched strong legs, black-and-white whiskers twitching. Morning air, damp earth, sweet clover, dewdrops like tiny diamonds. Birds popped and piped and trilled, a morning song that did not need extra verses. Today felt special. You could just feel it, the way clover smells when the dew is still deciding whether to stay.

Then a new sound. Ding-dong! Carwyn Button, the town crier, who usually just shouted, had a shiny brass bell that gleamed and a big fat notebook. Ding-dong, ding-dong. He cleared his throat. “A-hem!”

Bramble poked his head out, black nose twitching. Lila the mouse zipped across the grass, always ready for fun, and darted up Bramble’s snout to perch, tiny pink ears up. “What’s he saying?” Whiskers wiggling, so curious.

Carwyn, a badger too but quite thin, checked his notebook, tapped his quill. “Attention, town folk! The market is Saturday. Apples, plump and ready. Carrots, crisp and orange. Berries, sweet as sunshine.” He paused, squinted at the book. “And I have added extra notes. Extra information prevents bother!”

Lila giggled, a tiny fairy-bell sound. “Extra notes? What kind?”

“Indeed!” Serious now. “Apples: try Golden Pippins! Best for pies! A tartness that sings! Pick them by their stems. Firm stem means fresh. Loose? Maybe it fell. Nobody wants a bruised apple!”

Bramble blinked. This was taking too long. The sun climbed. His tummy grumbled. Lila bounced on his nose, tap-tap-tap. “He’s still talking about berries!”

Carwyn, lost in notes, kept going. “Berries: wild raspberries tasty today, they don’t last. Cultivated strawberries keep two, maybe three days. Keep them dry! Watch for ants — they like sweets too, but they’re not for sale.” He turned a page as if the page itself had asked to be read. “Timothy Tipple lost a bright blue marble near the old oak! Tiny, like a ladybug’s eye, swirls of white. Return it to his mother. Mrs. Tipple lives by the baker’s, cottage with the bright red door, flower boxes. Mrs. Buttercup the baker makes cinnamon buns, but this week lemon drizzle! Mr. Higgins the hedgehop tried a crumb, said it was sunshine and tang. Mr. Higgins also mentioned a second crumb, which is not news, and a third, which is even less—”

“Whoa!” Bramble’s boom cut through. “That’s a lot of extra notes! More notes than news!”

Lila, a tiny trumpet: “We know about Timothy’s marble! And Mrs. Buttercup’s cake! And the ants!”

Carwyn looked flustered, ears drooping. “But these are useful things! Isn’t a town crier supposed to be useful? Help everyone know everything?” He clutched the notebook as if the extra pages might still prove themselves.

Mayor Porth, a plump rabbit, waddled over, adjusted his glasses. “Your enthusiasm is grand. Truly. These announcements are… extensive. A whole day’s worth.”

Carwyn sighed. “I wanted to be extra, extra helpful. Nobody missing out. Ants. Mr. Higgins’ cakes.”

Bramble chuckled, a deep warm rumble. Lila wiggled. “You are helpful. Wonderfully. But maybe keep the main news snappy. Quick, like a robin’s morning call. Extra tips? Whisper to friends. Or write a special note.”

Lila’s tiny paws clapped. “A quiet tip! Only for curious ones!”

Carwyn’s ears perked. “A quiet tip? Efficient. Exciting.” The quill danced. “Market Saturday. Apples, carrots, berries. Lost marble for Timothy. That’s the news!” He grinned, winked. “Tell Mrs. Tipple Carwyn Button says hello. Timothy’s marble might be near a bright yellow dandelion. Dandelions are bright, just like his marble.”

Mayor Porth beamed. Worries melted. “The quick helpful news we need to start the day.”

Bramble’s heart felt bright as the sun. Sharing things the right size felt like a proper morning. “Ready for more?” he asked Lila.

“Always!” She bounced to his shoulder.

They dashed off, paws barely touching dewy grass, toward whatever the rest of the morning had decided to be without a list. He logged ding-dong / Golden Pippins / snappy-news in no notebook at all, left Carwyn the bell and a thinner page, and let Lila keep the dandelion tip as the first unofficial extra. The market, when Saturday came, still had apples, carrots, berries, and one marble that had been announced once, which was enough. Carwyn rang the bell twice and stopped, which was the useful part.
